title: Lesson 19 · Irregular Verbs & Capitals

items.prompt: What begins every sentence?
items.explain: Every sentence begins with a capital letter.

items.prompt: Which single words are always capitals?
items.explain: The single words “I” and “O” are always capitals.

items.prompt: A unipersonal verb (as in “It snows”) has what kind of subject?
items.explain: “it” stands in as an indefinite subject that names nothing in particular.

items.prompt: In “It rains,” what kind of verb is “rains”?
items.explain: It asserts an act with no real subject — a unipersonal verb.

items.prompt: An irregular verb does NOT form its past by doing what?
items.explain: Irregular verbs never add -ed; they change or stay the same instead.

items.prompt: Words made from proper names (American, French) take a ___.
items.explain: Words made from proper names take a capital letter.
